My Dutch quest

Who knew that I'd start with my first Dutch class in Taipei, and that now the quest would be to build a family in the Netherlands? Life is unpredictable! Follow along on my Dutch quest to see what I used at each level, which skills it trained, and the detours real life put in my way.

❗ This is my authentic experience, and there are affiliate links on this page. They cost you nothing extra, but they could support my work on this website and my content creation.

  1. A0
    2014–2017National Taiwan University, Taipei

    Where it began

    A0 → A1

    I first met Dutch at university in Taiwan, as my second foreign language. My teacher taught from the textbook Totaal, and that's where I learned the alphabet, how Dutch sounds, and the basics of grammar.

    In my backpack

    • Totaal: Basiscursus Nederlands · textbook (affiliate link)
      Self-paced
      • Listening
      • Reading
      • Writing
      • Grammar
      • Vocabulary
      More info

      For medium and highly educated non-Dutch speakers who understand English, German or French. For beginners, it gives a good vocabulary list and the grammar basics.

    • University Dutch classes · second foreign language
      In-person class · Schools and universities
      • Speaking
      • Listening
      • Reading
      • Writing
      • Pronunciation
      • Vocabulary
      • Confidence
      More info

      Taught by a native Dutch speaker who understands Mandarin and English. An interactive small class that lit up my interest in the Netherlands.

    Milestones

    • 🏆Set a good base of alphabet and pronunciation.
    • 🏆Qualified for a half-year exchange programme at Leiden University.

  5. A2
    Jul 2021 – 2022First job, Amsterdam

    The inburgering exam

    A2 ✓

    I started my first full-time job in Amsterdam and settled into life here. To pass the inburgering exam (A2), needed for citizenship, I did the official practice exams and wrote a diary in Dutch every day. My reading and writing improved a lot.

    In my backpack

    • Official practice exams · inburgeren.nl
      Self-paced · Government
      • Exam prep
    • A daily diary in Dutch
      Self-paced
      • Writing
      More info

      I kept this up for 30 days right before the exam, to train my writing.

    • Learn Dutch with Kim: A2 video course · bought in 2021 to prepare for the exam (affiliate link)
      Self-paced · Online courses
      • Listening
      • Reading
      • Grammar
      • Verbs
      • Vocabulary
      More info

      Very engaging and informative videos made by Kim. Besides her free videos on YouTube, buying this course gives you extra PDF materials explaining the grammar, more examples, exercises, quizzes, and extra stories with audio and transcripts. It suits learners on a smaller budget who enjoy self-paced study with videos and PDFs. She offers courses from A0 to B1.

    • Learn Dutch with Kim · YouTube channel
      Level A1 → A2 · Self-paced · YouTube
      • Listening
      • Grammar
    • Heb je zin? · Bart de Pau's series on YouTube
      Self-paced · YouTube
      • Listening

    Setbacks

    • ⛰️Busy settling into a new job and a new life

    Milestones

    • 🏆2022: passed the inburgering exam and got my certificate.
  6. ☁
    2022–2023Amsterdam

    Stuck on a plateau

    Plateau

    Day to day I still used English and only simple Dutch. I even stopped posting on Instagram for a while. I bought Nederlands in actie to study on my own, but couldn't keep it going.

    In my backpack

    • Nederlands in actie · self-study book (affiliate link)
      Level A2 → B1 · Self-paced
      • Reading
      • Grammar
      • Vocabulary
      More info

      Suitable if you like lots of reading material and enjoy looking up vocabulary yourself. Not the most engaging textbook. Each chapter has many assignments, and the appendix brings all the grammar rules together in a clearer way. It suits learners who are used to theoretical self-study.

    Setbacks

    • ⛰️Not enough self-discipline to study alone
    • ⛰️English for almost everything
  7. ✦
    2023My first own apartment

    A home worth investing in

    Turning point

    Moving into my own first apartment made me want to put real effort into Dutch again.

  8. A2
    End of 2024 – 2025Dutch in Utrecht

    Back to the classroom

    A2 → B1

    I signed up with Dutch in Utrecht: the studio was close to home, the price was affordable, and my neighbour recommended the teacher. Sometimes we went to class together, which made it fun. In class I practised speaking a lot, and with the book De Sprong I reviewed grammar in a short time.

    In my backpack

    • Dutch in Utrecht · private in-person lessons
      In-person class · Online tutors
      • Speaking
      • Listening
      • Pronunciation
      • Grammar
      • Confidence
      More info

      Private lessons where I could practise speaking and pronunciation a lot, review the grammar I had forgotten, and quickly learn anything I wanted. He offers courses for all levels.

    • De Sprong · textbook (affiliate link)
      Level A2 → B1 · Self-paced
      • Listening
      • Reading
      • Writing
      • Grammar
      • Vocabulary
      More info

      Colourful pages and a good mix of listening, reading, writing and speaking exercises if you use it in a class. It takes more space to explain the grammar rules than Nederlands in actie. Really good self-study material for levels A2 to B1.

    • A study buddy · my neighbour
      Practice groups
      • Speaking
      More info

      She has a similar Dutch level to mine, so luckily we could join the private lessons together, pay a cheaper rate, and have interesting conversations with the teacher.

    • Duolingo · at least one session every day since 2025
      All levels · Self-paced · Apps
      • Pronunciation
      • Vocabulary
      More info

      I only use the free version. One session a day doesn't take much effort, and sometimes you still learn something new from it.

    Milestones

    • 🏆2025: got Dutch citizenship, bought a house with my Dutch partner, and wanted to invest even more in my Dutch.
  9. A2
    Oct 2025 – 2026A new city with my partner

    All in: an intensive course

    B1

    I moved in with my partner in a new city. We plan to build a family in the Netherlands, so I decided to really invest time in Dutch. I joined NL Training's free, intensive, in-person course with the book Wind Mee. I learned many verbs in different tenses, more grammar, and found the courage to speak Dutch in daily life again. I also started a 365-day speaking challenge on Instagram, practising with my Dutch partner.

    In my backpack

    • NL Training · free intensive course
      Level A2 ✓ · In-person class · Schools and universities
      • Speaking
      • Listening
      • Writing
      • Grammar
      • Verbs
      • Confidence
      More info

      It offers free in-person courses under certain conditions. You can't choose your teacher, and your class depends on your level test and which groups have places left. It suits A1–A2 learners who want to progress further, because all communication is in Dutch. Their courses mainly cover A0 to A2, for integration (inburgering).

    • Wind Mee · textbook (affiliate link)
      Level A1 → A2 · Self-paced
      • Listening
      • Reading
      • Writing
      • Grammar
      • Verbs
      • Vocabulary
      More info

      A colourful, engaging self-study book for levels A1 to A2, with a good mix of reading, writing, listening and speaking exercises. The content is practical for everyday conversations, too.
